newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senate Environment Committee sets agenda.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senate Environment Committee sets agenda.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works Committee plans to take up the issue of controlling interstate waste as its first item of business when it resumes work this month, Committee Chairman John Chafee said in a statement.
Outlining the committee's agenda, the Rhode Island Republican said its next efforts will be to pass a new Intermodal Surface Transportation Efficiency bill before an October 1 deadline.

Chafee said the panel also will consider proposals to reform the Endangered Species Act and the Superfund hazardous waste cleanup law, as well as "targeted reforms" of the Clean Water Act, and its wetlands program.
The House last year passed a bill with sweeping changes to the Clean Water Act that the Clinton administration and environmental groups slammed as a rollback of pollution rules.
The Senate Environment Committee did not move a version of the bill.
Chafee said the committee also will hold oversight hearings on the Environmental Protection Agency's proposal to strengthen air quality standards on smog and soot pollution.

Subcommittee chairmen are John Warner, R-Virginia, for transportation and infrastructure; Bob Smith, R-New Hampshire, for Superfund, waste control and risk assessment; Dirk Kempthorne, R-Idaho, for drinking water, fisheries and wildlife; and James Inhofe, R-Oklahoma, for clean air, wetlands, private property and nuclear safety.
